{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-id-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ba75bb353c8e7cbf2086eb7781d3493c5c7947c73b027887e6681979d4976b70","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-id-class-d:lineage:36","source_registry_sha256":"9c432577e712960022ff656d6738a091319c6e5e4dcbdcf9429cd450e142e543","source_liveness_sha256":"eee60602368bd429216c9c2833be0be6ed9e505e5c5accebaefb9d2b9a847475"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Speed, stops, turns and right of way","heading":"C — Speed, stops, turns and right of way","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Speed, stops, turns and right of way

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A68
Idaho's basic speed rule requires a reasonable and prudent speed at all times, including roads with legal or posted maximum and minimum limits. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A68
Choose speed with regard to other traffic, pedestrians, bicycles, road surface, intersection hazards, visibility, oncoming traffic and curves. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A68
Driving too slowly for existing conditions while impeding safe traffic flow violates the basic speed rule even below the posted limit. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A68
The handbook's interstate maximum is seventy-five miles an hour unless a different limit is posted. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A68
An interstate limit of eighty miles an hour may be allowed where it is posted. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A68
The stated state-highway maximum is sixty-five miles an hour, with seventy allowed where posted. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A68
The maximum in a residential, business or urban district is thirty-five miles an hour unless posted otherwise. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A69
Do not drive so slowly that normal traffic flow is disrupted. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A69
Do not remain in the extreme left lane in a way that impedes traffic traveling at a lawful speed. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A69
Obey the posted speed limit in a school zone. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A69
Obey posted speed limits in designated work zones. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A69
A work-zone speed violation may result in an enhanced fixed penalty. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A69
Vehicle racing, speed exhibitions and speed contests are illegal on public roads, streets and highways. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A69
A flashing red indication requires stopping and is treated like a stop sign. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A69
A steady red arrow requires a stop and forbids a turn in the arrow's direction until a green or yellow indication allows it. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A69
At a steady circular red signal, stop completely and remain behind the stop line. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A69
If there is no stop line at a steady circular red signal, stop before entering the crosswalk. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A69
A green arrow displayed with a steady red indication permits movement only in the green arrow's direction. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A69
Except for a permitted red-light turn or movement authorized by a green arrow, wait for green before proceeding from a steady circular red. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A70
At an intersection, stop or slow as needed to yield to a pedestrian within a marked or unmarked crosswalk. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A70
Stop at a railway crossing for an approaching train or when a wigwag, flashing signal, gate or watchman indicates that a train is approaching. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A70
Before joining a street from a private road, driveway, building or alley, stop short of the sidewalk and yield to both pedestrians and other traffic. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A70
Stop when a police officer requests it. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A70
For an emergency or police vehicle using a siren or flashing red or blue lights, pull to the nearest right edge or curb clear of intersections and stay stopped until it passes or an officer permits movement. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A70
Stop when involved in a crash. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A70
For a school bus loading or unloading students, stop and remain stopped while its upper red lights flash or its stop arm is extended, except for opposite-direction traffic on a highway with four or more lanes and two lanes in each direction. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A70
A driver who has to stop for a school bus cannot move on until every child is clear of both the bus and the roadway. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A70
Opposite-direction traffic need not stop for the school bus on a highway with four or more lanes when two lanes go in each direction. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A71
When slowing or stopping, signal other drivers using the rear brake-operated lights or an arm signal. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A71
Travel speed affects the available reaction time and the time needed to stop. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A71
The handbook warns that excessive speed contributes to crashes and can combine dangerously with other violations, mechanical failures or judgment errors. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A71
When stopped behind another vehicle, a safe habit is to leave enough space to see where its rear tires touch the ground. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A71
Leaving the recommended stopped-vehicle gap may prevent striking the vehicle ahead if another vehicle hits from behind. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A71
The recommended stopped-vehicle gap may provide room to go around a stalled vehicle without backing into a traffic hazard. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0071]

Misconceptions: A red-light turn still requires a stop and yielding; the opposing school-bus exception depends on the stated lane configuration.
Mnemonic: Condition, control and clear is a teaching reminder to check the applicable rule before moving.
Glossary: The basic speed rule requires reasonable and prudent travel; right of way identifies who must yield; a posted exception changes the stated default rule.
Dynamic facts: installed limits, work-zone controls and posted turn prohibitions are not assigned invented local values.
